newsitem.title: USA: Closing arguments to continue in Simpson case.
newsitem.headline: Closing arguments to continue in Simpson case.

text.p: The jury in the O.J. Simpson civil trial is not expected to begin deliberations until at least Tuesday afternoon as closing arguments dragged on longer than expected on Monday.

Lawyers in the case said they expected plaintiffs' lawyer Daniel Petrocelli to wind up the rebuttal arguments Tuesday morning. Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki would then give instructions to the jury before handing them the case.
During Monday's session, Simpson's attorney Robert Baker wound up his closing argument, imploring the jury to "give Mr Simpson back his life."
Petrocelli and another plaintiffs' attorney Thomas Lambert then launched into a concerted effort to tear down the defense case.

"One blood drop is enough, one shoeprint is enough," said Petrocelli, who represents the family of victim Ronald Goldman, pointing out that Simpson's blood was found at the scene and that the blood of Goldman and Nicole Brown Simpson were found in the former football star's Ford Bronco.
Simpson was acquitted in 1995 of the June 12, 1994 murders. He is currently battling a wrongful death lawsuit brought by the families of the victims, who are seeking substantial damages.
